text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Jordanian press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- King Hussein stresses Jordan's rejection of any changes in Jerusalem that threaten the peace process; calls for the majority's word to be heard to confront a minority that tries to impose violence.

- Officials say Jordan has reservations over extraditing Hamas leader Abu Marzook now in a New York jail to the kingdom; but opens the door to a humanitarian solution to the case of the detained leader.
- Floods sweep three children away in Amman and Juweidah.
- King Hussein says Jerusalem "is a sensitive and very important issue" and expresses hope that people's emotions should not be inflamed.

- King Hussein warns in a joint news conference with visiting Israeli Prime Minisiter Benjamin Netanyahu of any actions that would disrupt the peace process; says the peace which Jordan is committed to is the one that builds a better future for coming generations.
- Stocks rebound after late buying orders with the official 60-share index bouncing back to 156.5 points.
- Zarqa mayor who was arrested on charges of slandering deputies is let free on bail and resumes work.
- King meets Arab Israeli Knesset members, reiterates support for Palestinian endeavours.
- King sends message to Libyan leader.
